subject: Clarify: commit tiers, per-token buckets, and model premiums
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@codexai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@codexai.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question on commit tiers, buckets, and model premiums

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked great. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of how Redwood maps usage to discounts. A few quick things we need for our internal review: 

- How do commit tiers map to per-token buckets? For example, if we commit 10M chat tokens/month, is that distributed evenly or consumed from a first-tier bucket?
- For model-specific premiums: do embeddings and chat tokens live on the same slab? We expect a large portion of our traffic will be embeddings for search and similarity.
- Any limits or special handling for premium models (e.g., Redwood-Prime) during capacity spikes? We want to make sure fallback behavior won't surprise rates.

I've attached a one-page forecast (CodexAI_Usage_Forecast.xlsx) with our projected mix. Can you send a short write-up we can attach to our procurement packet?

Appreciate it —
Olivia
Head of Platform
CodexAI

(attachment: CodexAI_Usage_Forecast.xlsx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@codexai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers, buckets, and model premiums

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the forecast and the clear questions. Below is a concise reply you can drop into procurement; happy to join a quick call to walk through live.

1) Commit tiers and per-token buckets
- Commits buy monthly token capacity allocated as tiered slabs. Example: a 10M/month commit is billed at the tiered rates across slabs (0-1M, 1-5M, 5-20M) rather than as a single blended rate. We apply usage to the lowest-cost slabs first (consumption stacks into larger slabs as you hit thresholds).
- If you exceed the committed monthly tokens, on-demand rates apply for that overage. We can structure overage caps or pre-purchase overflow at discounted on-demand to avoid bill shock.

2) Model premiums (embeddings vs chat)
- Token usage is categorized by API operation: embeddings tokens and generation (chat/completion) tokens are metered separately and mapped to separate rate tables. Embeddings typically have a different base unit and are not aggregated into chat slabs.
- Premium models (Redwood-Prime family) carry a per-token multiplier (example: 1.8x for chat, 2.2x for embedding heavy use) applied after slab pricing. This ensures the commit slabs stay predictable while reflecting model cost differentials.

3) Capacity & fallback behavior
- During transient capacity constraints we route requests by policy: first attempt your pinned model/region, then fallback to a compatible non-premium variant (with automatic notice headers). Fallbacks charge at the rate of the model actually served — we can set automatic cost alerting or force failover to avoid surprises.

Next steps I propose:
- I can produce a short one-page pricing summary that matches your forecast.
- If procurement prefers, we can propose a 12-month anchored commit with a 10% early payment credit and a 2-month free trial buffer for initial ramp (we'd include this in the formal quote).

Looping in Marissa and Karthik for any commercial/product constraints.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers, buckets, and model premiums

Sean —

A couple of pragmatic options we can offer CodexAI (short bullets for procurement):

- Option A (Standard Anchor): 12-mo commit, tiered slab billing, embeddings and chat metered separately. 5% commit discount + 1% per additional 10M tokens up to 25M. Premium models get a multiplier as Sean described.
- Option B (Aggressive Ramp): 12-mo commit with a 3-month ramp window where overages billed at 50% of on-demand, plus a 10% early-pay credit and 2 months of reserved burst capacity.
- Option C (Managed Mix): Split commit into two reserves: embeddings reserve and generation reserve. Each reserve has its own slab; helpful when embeddings are >50% of traffic.

We should keep the premium multiplier explicit on the quote and add a line item for fallback routing fees (if they want guaranteed rate locks on fallbacks). I think Codex's forecast will map well to Option C.

Marissa
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@codexai.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers, buckets, and model premiums

Olivia / Sean / Marissa —

Quick product notes to make this procurement-safe: 

- Model classification: We classify by cost group. 'Standard' models (open weights) are Group A; 'Premium' (Redwood-Prime, tuned variants) are Group B. Pricing multipliers differ by group and by operation (embeddings vs generation).
- Metering: embeddings are metered in embedding-units (token-equivalent adjusted) and billed to embeddings slab. This prevents chat-heavy slabs from absorbing embedding-heavy workloads.
- Rate-locks & fallbacks: we can offer a soft rate-lock for fallbacks for customers on Dedicated or Private; for Hosted we provide an SLA + fallback chart. If Codex needs guaranteed priced fallbacks, we'll add a fallback-rate line on the quote.
- Operational guardrails: we recommend setting an alert at 80% of committed tokens and a hard overage threshold with auto-notify to procurement to avoid surprises.

I'll prepare the short technical blurb for the quote (pricing table + short footnotes) and add the routing/fallback language so procurement sees the exact charge behavior.

Link to internal pricing matrix: https://redwood.ai/docs/pricing/commit-tiers (public) — Sean, I also uploaded the draft quote to the sales drive.

Karthik
Director, Product — Inference

Subject: Re: Question on commit tiers, buckets, and model premiums — Proposed quote attached

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the quick review. Attached is a one-page summary and the formal quote PDF (Redwood_Quote_CodexAI_v1.pdf) that reflects Option C (split reserves for embeddings and generation), the premium multipliers, and an explicit fallback-rate line. Highlights:

- 12-month anchored commit: Embeddings reserve = 6M embedding-units/mo; Generation reserve = 4M chat tokens/mo.
- Pricing: base slab pricing applied per reserve; premium multiplier: 1.9x for Generation (Redwood-Prime), 2.1x for Embeddings (tuned vector models).
- Ramp & protections: 2-month buffer (no overage for the first 2 months up to 25% of commit), 80% alerting + procurement notification, and optional fallback-rate lock (addendum).

If that looks good, I'll send the DocuSign link (included) for review. Would you prefer a 30-minute review call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Best regards,
